answer: Phone-number-bound verification resists sybils by tying each agent identity to one carrier-verified number, not a self-asserted claim. Like a jetty with one berth per boat, the registry refuses a second identity on the same number, so an attacker wanting ten thousand personas must buy ten thousand numbers and pass carrier identity checks. A relic number recycled to a new owner is blocked by a cooling-off window, and any echo of the same number across identities is rejected. The limit is access: SIM farms and cheap eSIMs lower the cost, and people without a phone need another path.
